business_summary.text: Tenneco Clean Air India Limited is a manufacturer of clean air and powertrain solutions and advanced ride technologies (suspension systems) for passenger and commercial vehicles, with 12 locations in India.

call_points.text: Order book will now be reported half-yearly; H1FY27 figure due at Q2, with domestic and export split.
Won four new customers for conventional and DCx suspension, plus a spark plug order from a large PV OEM; values not disclosed.
Margin decline of 170 bps YoY attributed to listed-company costs and non-indexed commodity inflation; only partial recovery so far.
Royalty at 2.5% of overall revenue reduced by intercompany sales, consistent with the prior year.
US Section 232 tariffs on some exhaust parts and weak Europe/Americas demand are headwinds for exports.
Analyst asked for segment-wise margin decline; CFO declined, saying the company does not disclose BU-level margins.
BS-VII plus CAFE 3 seen lifting content per vehicle only 1.3x-1.5x, far below the BS-IV to BS-VI jump.
Two new plants (North India Clean Air, West India ART) represent announced capex of about ₹140 Cr; commissioning in six months to a year.
Exports are 5-6% of sales but 14-20% of order book; management expects critical mass around 2028.
Debt-free with net debt-to-equity of negative 0.4; cash flow equivalent to 58% of EBITDA after ₹115 Cr capex.
Localisation at 89-90%; management aims to maintain this level as new technologies are introduced.

operating_notes.text: Lifetime order book of ₹12,400 Cr as of 31 March 2026 provides 100% visibility of FY28 internal revenue target.
Exports are 5-6% of sales but 14-20% of order book; management expects critical mass around 2028.
Localisation at 89-90%; CAFE 3 and BS7 present ₹1,300-1,400 Cr additional addressable content opportunity.
Capacity utilisation was above 80% for Clean Air & Powertrain and above 90% for Advanced Ride Technologies in Q1FY27.
Exports were just over 7% of Q1FY27 revenue, up from about 5% pre-IPO, with the export order book split 70% Tenneco-to-Tenneco and 30% third-party OEMs.
Royalty is 2.5% of overall revenue reduced by intercompany sales, in line with the previous year.
